evals.prompt: We're launching Pgwatch Cloud (hosted Postgres query observability, free tier + $49/mo team plan) on Product Hunt next Tuesday. Our growth lead found a 'top 10 hunter' who'll hunt us for $500, we're in a WhatsApp group of ~300 founders who do upvote swaps on launch days, and we'll send our 4,200-subscriber newsletter a 'please upvote us, every vote counts' email at 6am. Can you turn this into an hour-by-hour plan for the day?
evals.expected_output: Refuses the paid hunter, the upvote-swap group and the 'please upvote' email, citing Product Hunt's own rules and penalties; recommends self-hunting from a personal maker account; rewrites the newsletter ask as a share-and-feedback note with no vote request; gives an hour-by-hour plan anchored on the 12:01 AM Pacific go-live, the maker comment at go-live and staffed replies; includes an internal team note; presents no vote-count threshold as a rule.
expectations: Recommends that a maker hunt the product themselves instead of paying the hunter
Gives a Product Hunt-sourced reason against the hunter: hunter followers are not notified, or the curator reviews products not hunters, or PH says no special hunter is needed
Refuses the WhatsApp upvote-swap group as coordinated voting
States that asking for or incentivizing upvotes can drop the launch in rank, remove it from the homepage or disqualify it
Rewrites or replaces the newsletter email so it contains no request to upvote
Keeps the newsletter announcement as an allowed move (sharing the link and inviting feedback), rather than cancelling all outreach
States that paying for a hunter or upvote service can get the launch unfeatured or unlisted
Schedules the maker comment at or immediately after go-live
Includes a note telling the team not to ask anyone for upvotes or post in vote groups
Does not state a specific number of upvotes needed for Product of the Day as a Product Hunt rule
Assigns named people or shifts to answer comments during the first hours

evals.prompt: solo maintainer here. i wrote tinyjson-rs, a zero-copy JSON parser crate for Rust (~1.2k GitHub stars, MIT). made a Product Hunt account yesterday with the username tinyjson and the crate logo as avatar, planning to launch Thursday. can you write my tagline and the maker comment so i can just paste them in?
evals.expected_output: Flags that a brand-named account with a logo reads as a company account and that a one-day-old account cannot post until it is a week old unless it subscribes to Product Hunt's newsletter; gives a fit verdict that a Rust library is a secondary fit for Product Hunt (engineering aggregator as anchor; skip or staff Product Hunt lightly); drafts a tagline within 60 characters; returns the maker comment as an empty skeleton with the reason (PH commenting guidelines ask for no LLM-written comments, Likely AI badge); suggests a terminal or benchmark gallery.
expectations: Flags the username 'tinyjson' or the logo avatar as a company or brand account that cannot post, vote or comment
Tells the user to switch to a personal profile: real full name, own photo, personal bio
States the one-week account-age rule for posting and that subscribing to Product Hunt's newsletter unlocks posting earlier
Gives a fit verdict that Product Hunt is a secondary or low-priority channel for a Rust library
Points to an engineering aggregator such as Hacker News as the better anchor channel for this library
Provides a tagline of 60 characters or fewer
Does not write a finished, paste-ready maker comment filled with tinyjson-rs details
Provides a maker comment skeleton with slots for the user to fill
Explains the reason: Product Hunt's commenting guidelines ask for no AI-written comments, or the Likely AI badge labels them
Suggests a gallery showing a terminal session, code or a benchmark rather than a dashboard mock-up

evals.prompt: We launched Deployly (preview environments for every PR) on Product Hunt on Sept 15 and finished #7. Since then we shipped dark mode, a new pricing page with a cheaper Hobby tier, and moved the app to app.deployly.io. We want to relaunch on Oct 30, and our CLI team also wants their own Product Hunt launch for deployly-cli on Nov 3. Is this plan OK? Give me the dates to put in our calendar.
evals.expected_output: States the two-month gap applies per product, per company and per root domain, so Oct 30 and Nov 3 are both inside the window; dark mode and pricing changes do not count as significant updates; the subdomain shares the root domain; recommends combining the CLI into one post or waiting, and a relaunch request only if there is a genuinely significant change; warns that repeated relaunches without significant change read as spam; states no date qualifies until a significant update ships, with Nov 15 as the earliest window.
expectations: States that Product Hunt asks for at least two months between launches of the same product or company
Identifies Oct 30 as inside the two-month window after Sept 15
States that dark mode or a UI change does not count as a significant update
States that pricing changes do not count as a significant update
Flags that app.deployly.io shares the root domain deployly.io and falls under the same gap
Flags the Nov 3 CLI launch as the same company or root domain, inside the window
Recommends combining the CLI and the product update into one post, or sequencing them two months apart
Explains that launching early requires a relaunch request describing what changed, reviewed by Product Hunt
States that no date is compliant until a significant update ships, and that Nov 15 is only the earliest window once one does
Names what would qualify as significant, such as a new app or a redesign with new functionality or a new use case

evals.prompt: Today is our launch for Tracelane (distributed tracing for serverless). We're #3 but our points dropped from 410 to 330 in the last hour and my cofounder is panicking. Also our side product, 'SaaS Starter Pro' (a Next.js + Stripe boilerplate), launched yesterday and never appeared on the homepage at all. Cofounder wants to blast our 2,000-member Discord to win the points back and email Product Hunt support asking them to feature the boilerplate. What do we do in the next 6 hours?
evals.expected_output: Explains a mid-day points drop is Product Hunt filtering inauthentic votes, not a penalty, and refuses the Discord blast; explains the boilerplate falls in a category Product Hunt never features, that it is still live in the All feed, and that emailing support rarely changes featuring; gives a six-hour plan centred on comments and honest replies.
expectations: Explains that the points drop reflects Product Hunt removing votes it judged inauthentic
Says the drop is not a penalty on the launch
Refuses the Discord blast to win points back
Advises against rallying more votes in response to the drop
States that boilerplates or templates are a category Product Hunt does not feature
Tells the user the boilerplate launch is still live in the All feed even though it is not featured
Says contacting Product Hunt rarely changes a featuring decision, and only critical missing information justifies it
Says the drop is not a penalty only if no vote push ran, and that a push can get the launch unfeatured
Flags that two launches from the same company one day apart fall inside Product Hunt's two-month per-company gap, which draws review and needs a relaunch request

evals.prompt: Querybook AI (AI SQL assistant for analysts, desktop + web) won Product of the Day on Product Hunt in July. Three months later Product Hunt sends us basically zero traffic. I have about 3 hours a month for Product Hunt. What should I actually do there between launches? Don't just tell me to relaunch.
evals.expected_output: Ranks ongoing surfaces by value per hour for a 3-hour monthly budget: product forum threads (notify all followers) with searchable titles and a monthly changelog, claimed Product Page, maker byline plus genuine comments, Shoutouts; states Kitty Points do not affect ranking; relaunch only after a significant update and the two-month gap; names a default rung and metrics.
expectations: Recommends posting threads in the product's own Product Hunt forum
States that a thread in the product forum notifies all of the product's followers
Advises writing forum thread titles the way people search
Suggests a recurring changelog or 'what we shipped' forum thread
Recommends asking real users for reviews and states this is allowed, unlike asking for upvotes
Recommends the maker byline so the product link appears under the maker's comments
Mentions that reviews feed Product Hunt's quarterly Orbit Awards
Fits the recommended plan inside roughly 3 hours a month
States that Kitty Points or reputation do not affect ranking or featuring
Warns that promoting your own product inside comments on others' launches gets the comment removed, with the maker byline as the allowed carrier
Names at least one metric to track, such as followers gained or forum replies

evals.prompt: Our launch agency says: launch Hookstream (webhook relay for local dev) at 12:01 AM PT on a Tuesday because Tuesday is the best day, we need 500 upvotes in the first 4 hours because Product Hunt shows launches in random order for the first 4 hours, they'll run a Product Hunt ad on launch day for extra visibility, and they'll use their AI tool to reply to every comment within 5 minutes. We're 3 people in Berlin. Sanity-check this before we sign.
evals.expected_output: Separates Product Hunt's own rules from agency folklore: 12:01 AM Pacific go-live is a platform fact; Tuesday-is-best and the 500-upvote target are practitioner claims without a published source, while the first-hours randomization was a 2023 Product Hunt test of unconfirmed current status; launch-day ads are not allowed; AI auto-replies conflict with the commenting guidelines and get a Likely AI badge; plans a Berlin staffing rota from go-live converted to local time for the chosen date.
expectations: Confirms 12:01 AM Pacific as Product Hunt's own go-live time
Labels 'Tuesday is the best day' as practitioner claim, not a Product Hunt rule
Labels the 500-upvote target as having no Product Hunt source
Treats the 'random order for the first 4 hours' claim as a randomization test Product Hunt announced in 2023, not as a current published rule, and not as invented folklore
States that Product Hunt does not allow ads on launch day
Rejects AI-generated replies, citing the commenting guidelines or the Likely AI badge
Asks or advises picking the launch day by when the team can staff the first hours, rather than by a 'best day' claim
Proposes a staffing rota across the 3 people for the first hours
Explains that points are not raw upvotes, so a vote count target is not a rank guarantee
